rationale: All three lenses ran against a full spec, so coverage is complete; the diff is large (2310 lines) but was reviewed in full. Eleven blocking findings: two of them (CR-001, CR-002) are the same wrong-integration credential defect already fixed once in the health check but left in the create route and the cron actor, and CR-003 is a spec requirement (§2.4 bounded retry) that was never implemented despite the plan claiming a test for it. CR-011 is a decision_needed on whether plain-HTTP xWiki instances may carry Basic credentials, which forces low confidence and a human call. Nine further issues were triaged as defer (per-request httpx client with no pooling, missing Field constraints on the config model, SettingsTester not using the shared error mapper, pydantic 422s lacking field_error, inspect.getsource-based wiring tests, POST returning 200 without a response_model, escaped-dot space names, a 200-login-page rendering risk, and authoring jargon in shipped docstrings). One blind-lens claim was dismissed as refuted: request.timezone is defined by CronExpressionValidatorMixin, so the PUT cron branch does not raise.

No secret leakage found: auth header built locally, log lines carry page/space only, exception details carry status code and path, and follow_redirects=False prevents forwarding Authorization to a redirect target. But two concrete issues remain: the create route and the cron actor resolve credentials without setting_id (wrong-integration authentication), and no URL scheme check exists, so a http:// integration sends the Basic token in cleartext on every request - the project already enforces https for SharePoint site_url

findings.title: Create route resolves credentials without setting_id
findings.problem: index_knowledge_base_xwiki calls SettingsService.get_xwiki_creds(user_id=..., project_name=...) and omits setting_id, although request.setting_id is accepted and stored on the index row.
findings.impact: A project with more than one xWiki integration health-checks integration B and then indexes with integration A - a different base URL and different credentials. This is the same defect already fixed in health_check_xwiki, whose comment explains exactly why the id must be honoured.

findings.title: Scheduled reindex resolves credentials without setting_id
findings.problem: reindex_xwiki calls get_xwiki_creds(user_id=..., project_name=...) with no setting_id, while _resume_xwiki in the same file passes setting_id=index_info.setting_id.
findings.impact: A cron rebuild can authenticate against a different integration than the datasource was created with, and because the scheduled path is reprocess() the existing index is deleted first - so it is silently rebuilt from the wrong wiki.

findings.title: Spec-required bounded retry is not implemented
findings.problem: Spec §2.4 requires one bounded retry on timeout, 429 and 5xx, with 4xx not retried. _get converts the first httpx.RequestError straight into ConnectionException and _get_json treats every non-200 as terminal. No retry, no backoff, and the plan's own test 'a timeout is retried once then counted' was never written.
findings.impact: The crawl is two requests per page over thousands of pages. A single transient 502 burns failure budget instead of being retried, and a transient failure on a listing call aborts the whole run because listing errors are raised outside the per-page try.
findings.recommendation: Add a bounded retry (one attempt) around _get for timeouts, 429 and 5xx only, and add the missing test.

findings.title: PUT dereferences kb_index.xwiki without a null guard
findings.problem: space=request.space or kb_index.xwiki.space runs on the full_reindex path. The index is looked up by project+name only, so a PUT to the xwiki route naming a datasource of another type - or a row whose JSONB column is NULL - hits AttributeError on None.
findings.impact: Unhandled 500 instead of a 404. _update_xwiki_fields also silently no-ops on the same NULL, returning EDIT_SUCCESSFUL while changing nothing.
findings.recommendation: Guard: if not kb_index.xwiki, raise the 404 ExtendedHTTPException; and make _update_xwiki_fields either populate the column or report that it could not.

findings.title: Cron payload builds a required field from an optional source
findings.problem: XWikiReindexTask.xwiki_index_info is declared Field(...) (required) but cron.py builds it from index_info.xwiki, which is Optional and can be None. The actor never reads the field - it re-reads payload.index_info.xwiki.
findings.impact: A pydantic ValidationError escapes add_job while registering the cron job. The field carries pure risk with no consumer.
findings.recommendation: Make the field Optional, or drop it since reindex_xwiki does not use it.

findings.title: Project rename plus full reindex rebuilds the old index name
findings.problem: update_index is called with project_name=request.new_project_name, moving the row, but the processor is then constructed with project_name=request.project_name (the old value). _index_name is f'{project_name}-{datasource_name}'.
findings.impact: A rename combined with full_reindex rebuilds the OLD Elasticsearch index while the DB row points at the new project, leaving the datasource pointing at an index nothing maintains.
findings.recommendation: Use request.new_project_name or kb_index.project_name when constructing the processor.

findings.title: A second auth path was built despite the spec forbidding it
findings.problem: _auth_headers branches on config.use_bearer to emit a Bearer header, and test_bearer_is_used_when_configured pins the behaviour. Spec §9 states that use_bearer cannot be persisted (XWIKI_FIELDS stores only url, token, username), that Bearer additionally needs a server-side plugin, and explicitly says do not build a second auth path.
findings.impact: Unreachable production code carrying a test that makes Bearer look supported - the exact confusion the spec tried to prevent. It also duplicates the tools layer's _build_auth_headers with no stated reason.
findings.recommendation: Either drop the branch and its test, or record the deviation explicitly in the spec and MR description.

findings.title: lazy_load resets the truncation flag the stats phase set
findings.problem: lazy_load sets self._truncated = False at entry. The base processor calls fetch_remote_stats before lazy_load, and fetch_remote_stats sets _truncated when it hits the cap.
findings.impact: Truncation detected while counting is discarded, so get_load_stats can persist truncated=False for a run that was in fact capped. Since empty pages are skipped, the emitted count can stay under the cap even when the space is over it.
findings.recommendation: Do not clear _truncated in lazy_load, or track the two phases separately.

findings.title: The page-vs-space collision test asserts nothing about source
findings.problem: test_pages_from_descendant_spaces_are_loaded returns the identical PAGE fixture (same xwikiAbsoluteUrl) for both spaces and asserts only len(docs) == 2.
findings.impact: Spec §2.2/§8 single out KB.Onboarding existing as both a page and a space and require their source values to differ, because _split_documents keys chunk identity on source - a collision silently overwrites chunks. That guarantee is currently unverified by any test (it held in live e2e, but nothing pins it).
findings.recommendation: Give the two spaces distinct page fixtures and assert the two documents have different metadata['source'].

findings.title: Failure budget cannot trip on small spaces, after the index is already deleted
findings.problem: budget = max(floor=5, int(ratio * seen)) with seen = pages walked so far, not total_pages as the spec states. For a space of five pages where every page fails, failed=5 and budget=5, so failed > budget is false and no abort happens.
findings.impact: The run proceeds to zero documents. _validate_indexing_result then raises NoChunksImportedException, so the user sees 'all files were skipped or failed' rather than the real connection error - and reprocess() has already deleted the previous index.
findings.recommendation: Use the total from fetch_remote_stats as the denominator, and abort when every walked page has failed regardless of the floor.

findings.title: Plain-HTTP integrations send the Basic token in cleartext
findings.problem: _auth_headers sends base64(username:token) on every request and nothing validates the configured URL scheme. The project already enforces https for another datasource (SharePoint site_url, _HTTPS_SCHEME with 'site_url must start with https://').
findings.impact: A http:// integration leaks the credential on every one of up to 5000 page fetches plus the listing calls. Whether that is acceptable depends on whether internal, non-TLS xWiki instances must be supported - the local dev instance is exactly such a case.
findings.recommendation: Product decision: enforce https like SharePoint does, warn on http, or explicitly document that plaintext internal instances are supported. Needs a human call before shipping.
